entries.name: mcp__plugin_paper-desktop_paper__move_nodes
entries.description:
Move one or more existing nodes. Preserves node identity (IDs stay the same), so any references you are holding continue to work. Prefer this over duplicate+delete or rewriting HTML when you just want to reposition or reparent existing layers.

Each move uses one of two shapes:
1. Sibling-relative: { nodeId, before: siblingId } or { nodeId, after: siblingId }. The destination parent is inferred from the sibling.
2. Parent-absolute: { nodeId, parentId, index? }. The node is placed at the given index under parentId, or appended if index is omitted. index is clamped to [0, childCount] — use 0 for first. Pass parentId: 'root' as a shortcut for the page root of the page the node currently lives on.

Use shape sibling-relative shape 1 when you already know a neighbor; use parent-absolute shape 2 when you want to move into a specific parent (or to the end of one).

Notes:
- Moves apply sequentially; later moves in the same batch see earlier changes.
- For flex/flow parents this changes visual order. For freeform parents this changes stacking (last child renders on top) and does not move the node's world position.
- When moving to a new parent, Paper may adjust layout-related styles (width/height intents like filling available space) may be adjusted so the node does not collapse to zero size in the new parent.
- You can move nodes between pages
- Cannot move the root. Cannot target a node that cannot have children. Cannot move a node under itself or any of its own descendants. For before/after, the sibling cannot be the moved node itself.
Returns resolved parentId and index for each successful move, plus affectedParents — the post-batch children list of every parent whose order changed (both sources and destinations, deduplicated). Use affectedParents to refresh your mental model of the tree without a follow-up get_children.

nodeId.description: The ID of the node to move.

before.description: Place the node immediately before this sibling. The target parent is inferred from the sibling.

nodeId.description: The ID of the node to move.

after.description: Place the node immediately after this sibling. The target parent is inferred from the sibling.

nodeId.description: The ID of the node to move.

parentId.description: The ID of the destination parent. Must be able to have children (e.g. Frames). Pass the string `'root'` as a shortcut for the page root of the page the node currently lives on (same as that page's rootNodeId from get_basic_info).

index.description: The final index among the destination parent's children. Clamped to [0, childCount]. Use 0 for first, or omit to append at the end.

moves.description: Move operations, applied sequentially. Each operation sees the updated tree from prior operations.

fileId.description: The file ID that the tool should operate on.

entries.name: mcp__plugin_paper-desktop_paper__rename_pages
entries.description: Rename one or more pages in the file. Sets the display name shown in the page list. Does not switch which page the user is viewing. Supports batch renames in a single call.

pageId.description: The ID of the page to rename. Use get_basic_info to list pages.

name.description: The new display name for the page (shown in the page list).

updates.description: Array of rename updates. Each item specifies a page ID and its new name.

fileId.description: The file ID that the tool should operate on.

entries.name: mcp__plugin_paper-desktop_paper__set_text_content
entries.description: Set the text content of one or more Text nodes. Only works on nodes with component type "Text". Use this instead of writeHTML replace when you only need to change text. Supports batch updates in a single call.

nodeId.description: The ID of the Text node to update.

updates.description: Array of text updates to apply. Each item specifies a node ID and its new text content.

fileId.description: The file ID that the tool should operate on.

entries.name: mcp__plugin_paper-desktop_paper__update_styles
entries.description:
Update styles on one or more nodes. Use this for targeted style changes. Supports design tokens as CSS variables. Supports batch updates in a single call.
- Setting the top / left styles of an artboard changes its position on the canvas.
- Anywhere urls are accepted, paper-gen:// URLs can be used to generate images with AI. ONLY use when the user explicitly asked for image generation. Read "image-generation" guide first via get_guide.
- Styles you set that are inert in the node's context are dropped rather than applied; their keys are returned under the ignoredStyles property.

nodeIds.description: The IDs of the nodes to update.

styles.description: Styles as a JSON object with camelCase property names (e.g. {"backgroundColor": "#fff", "padding": "20px"}), like React.CSSProperties.

updates.description: Array of style updates to apply. Each item specifies node IDs and styles to apply to all of them.

fileId.description: The file ID that the tool should operate on.

entries.name: mcp__plugin_paper-desktop_paper__write_html
entries.description:
IMPORTANT: Write incrementally. The user sees you write on the canvas in real-time. Show them visual progress every few seconds. Each write_html call should create one visual item: a header, a single list row, a button bar, or a paragraph block. Even simple components should be incremental: a card = container/header, then each row, then the footer. IMPORTANT: Prefer cloning instead of remaking existing Paper nodes using ``. For repeated elements: create the container first, then add each item as a separate write_html call into the container or use the duplicate tool on the first child. HTML and CSS rules: - Always use inline styles (style="..") - Enforce consistency with design tokens as CSS variables if available - All Google Fonts and locally installed fonts are available in font-family - All CSS color formats are supported: hex, rgb(a), hsl(a), oklch, oklab etc - Use flex as the primary layout mode. Flexbox, padding, and gap are the core layout tools in Paper's interface - Absolute position is fully supported. Use it for decorative elements. Avoid covering the entire artboard with a single absolute element, it blocks cursor interaction underneath - Do NOT use: margin, display: inline, display: grid, HTML tables. Use padding and gap for spacing - display: block is acceptable for simple elements (text, decorative shapes) but not for layout containers - Assume border-box sizing everywhere - Use 
 or white-space: pre for code blocks or indented text
- Do NOT use emojis as icons. Use SVG icons or images
- Rich text isn't supported in Paper; code snippets should be a single element with one text color and pre whitespace
- Use the layer-name attribute to set names on elements in the Paper layer tree, e.g. 

- Local images MUST use absolute paths in an img starting with paper-asset:// e.g. 
- paper-gen:// URLs generate AI images. ONLY if the user asked; read the "image-generation" guide first

html.description: HTML string to parse into design nodes. Supports standard HTML elements with inline CSS styles.

targetNodeId.description: The ID of the target node. In "insert-children" mode, new nodes are added as children of this node. In "replace" mode, this node is removed and replaced by the parsed HTML.

mode.description: "insert-children" adds the HTML as children of the target node. "replace" removes the target node and puts the parsed HTML in its place.

fileId.description: The file ID that the tool should operate on.

DIRECTION CONCEPT SEED (key: 695e75bd; mode: experience; source: api; approved pool: c3b204a1eed6; 306/564 human-approved; rerun with --scope direction --mode experience --from 695e75bd --candidate-count 7 to reproduce this roll against this catalog revision)
ASSIGNED INDEX: 4
  After ordering the grounded directions by resonance, build candidate
  4 of your own grounded list; the assignment never points at a
  challenger. The assignment is the roll, not a suggestion: your top-ranked
  direction is what every run would ship, so the script decides which grounded
  direction gets built. Each direction joins a durable visual system to a
  concrete expression for the requested first surface, decided as one. It must
  survive the current task plus navigation, quiet and dense content,
  interaction and state, and a substantially different future surface. In an
  attended run, present the assigned direction fully committed and offer
  re-roll. You may add ONE card for your top-ranked grounded candidate when
  it is not the assigned direction, kicker IMPECCABLE’S PICK, with an honest risk line
  naming its familiarity; one pick card, never a ranked lineup, and the pick
  never takes the lead position. When the assignment IS your top candidate,
  there is no pick card. Re-roll yourself only
  on named factual grounds, when the assignment cannot carry the product's
  truth or task; taste is never grounds.
  The assignment exists to refuse the model's ranking rut, never to outrank
  the user or the brief. Never expose assignment metadata in user-facing labels.
CHALLENGERS:
  1. a moon-shadow bazaar, where merchants trade shadows by length, memory, temperature, and the strange light that cast them
     SOURCE ID: dream-surreal-impossible-worlds-moon-shadow-bazaar
     CREATIVE SPARK: A vendor unrolls the cool shadow of a cedar at midnight, another offers a child's summer silhouette in a glass jar, and the moon changes price by moving behind a cloud.
     SYSTEM GRAMMAR:
       - Palette/material: moonlit blue-black lane as ground, shadow goods in layered soft blacks, stall canvas in muted saffron, one cool moon white edging the active trade
       - Type/composition: bazaar signpainter script over chalked price caps, stalls ranked down one lane, each shadow tagged with a small ticket of origin and length
       - Topology/navigation: Wander stalls by shadow origin, shape, time, emotional charge, and possible exchange.
       - Controls/state: Cast, stretch, compare, trade, and return a shadow while its story stays attached.
       - Responsive/motion: Arrange stalls as a moonlit vertical lane on phones and retain high-contrast readable commerce.
     WEB LEVERAGE: Camera silhouette capture, solar geometry, and interactive shadow deformation turn personal light moments into ephemeral tradable artifacts.
     QUALITY BAR: board https://impeccable.style/worlds/cards/dream-surreal-impossible-worlds-moon-shadow-bazaar.webp · hero https://impeccable.style/worlds/cards/dream-surreal-impossible-worlds-moon-shadow-bazaar-hero.webp
  2. a home sewing pattern envelope and its tissue, fashion figures in three lettered views on the front, yardage tables on the back, and inside a folded map of dashed cutting lines, notches, grain arrows, and place-on-fold brackets
     SOURCE ID: fashion-folded-worlds-sewing-pattern-envelope
     CREATIVE SPARK: You smooth the crackling tissue across the table, third size line from the edge, and pin piece 4 with its grain arrow dead parallel to the fold before the scissors commit you to view B.
     SYSTEM GRAMMAR:
       - Palette/material: manila tissue ground with black drafting marks, envelope figures in dry gouache pastels, one dressmaker red tracing the view and size you have committed to
       - Type/composition: view letters A, B, and C rank the variants, circled piece numbers sit on every tissue shape, instructions run as numbered steps with thumbnail diagrams
       - Topology/navigation: the envelope front indexes the views, the back holds size and yardage tables, and the cutting layout maps every numbered piece onto the folded yardage
       - Controls/state: the chosen size renders its nested cut line solid while other sizes stay dashed, notches must meet to join pieces, and a placed piece pins flat and stops drifting
       - Responsive/motion: the layout refolds to the fabric width at hand, pieces never rotating off grain; motion is tissue settling and a pin dropping home
     WEB LEVERAGE: css outlines trace nested size grading while drag interaction snaps svg pieces onto a grain-locked layout grid
     QUALITY BAR: board https://impeccable.style/worlds/cards/fashion-folded-worlds-sewing-pattern-envelope.webp · hero https://impeccable.style/worlds/cards/fashion-folded-worlds-sewing-pattern-envelope-hero.webp
  3. a school-uniform subculture's dress code as a coded document, a lengthened pleated skirt and shortened sailor top annotated with rule callouts, group affiliation carried by embroidered collar stripes
     SOURCE ID: pop-culture-shelf-sukeban-long-skirt-code
     CREATIVE SPARK: the skirt lengthened by exactly this much, the top shortened by exactly that much, every deviation measured and annotated, and the stripe on the collar telling you who she answers to.
     SYSTEM GRAMMAR:
       - Palette/material: navy serge and white cotton with a single embroidered stripe color per group, matte cloth with no shine anywhere
       - Type/composition: annotated rule callouts on leader lines to each modification, a plain condensed sans for labels, and a stripe key ruled at the foot
       - Topology/navigation: the garment is a document, so navigation follows a leader line from a modification to the rule that governs it
       - Controls/state: controls are modifications, the active one draws its leader and rule, and non-conforming ones are marked with a struck line
       - Responsive/motion: callouts reposition around the figure at any width, and motion is a leader line drawing out to its label
     WEB LEVERAGE: an svg figure with animated leader-line callouts, responsive callout repositioning, and conformance state per modification
     QUALITY BAR: board https://impeccable.style/worlds/cards/pop-culture-shelf-sukeban-long-skirt-code.webp · hero https://impeccable.style/worlds/cards/pop-culture-shelf-sukeban-long-skirt-code-hero.webp
  4. a push pin studios poster, victorian and nouveau contours revived in flat candy color, an aubergine silhouette crowned with ribboned rainbow hair, illustrated warmth on modern structure
     SOURCE ID: brand-identity-canon-push-pin-poster
     CREATIVE SPARK: you unfold the poster from the record sleeve and a jet black profile blooms into ribbons of pink, teal, and orange hair, each lock a flat cut of candy color with no shadow anywhere
     SYSTEM GRAMMAR:
       - Palette/material: cream poster stock ground, flat candy fills of pink teal marigold and lilac, one jet black silhouette anchoring, the active item takes the warmest fill
       - Type/composition: hand-drawn slab and nouveau display lettering for titles, tidy modern text below, ornament framed inside clear geometric structure
       - Topology/navigation: one emblematic silhouette anchors each section and smaller vignettes orbit it, you move between posters, not pages
       - Controls/state: flat fills swap hue on state with no shading, hover blooms one more ribbon from the silhouette, disabled art drops to single-line contour
       - Responsive/motion: vignettes fold under the anchor silhouette on small screens; ribbons unfurl as drawn paths
     WEB LEVERAGE: svg paths carry the contour line art; css flat fills recolor per state without gradients
     QUALITY BAR: board https://impeccable.style/worlds/cards/brand-identity-canon-push-pin-poster.webp · hero https://impeccable.style/worlds/cards/brand-identity-canon-push-pin-poster-hero.webp
  5. A film cutting bench flattened into a sheet: a perforated select rail crossing a grain-orange field, each step a punched frame held between two pins, the place you stopped marked by a folded tape flag, and everything set aside still hanging on pins below the rail.
     SOURCE ID: operate-a-cutting-bench-select-rail
     CREATIVE SPARK: A work print strung between two pins under a bench lamp, white grease crosses struck across three frames, a folded orange tape flag doubled over the perforation where the editor stopped, and a dozen trims hanging on pins in the bin below.
     SYSTEM GRAMMAR:
       - Palette/material: one ink, flag orange in coarse film grain on true black; orange holds a third of any screen. Running copy and foreign images sit only in punched white windows.
       - Type/composition: one size of condensed grotesk throughout, caps for labels; rank is cell count not size, a window may span twelve frame cells while edge ticks stay hairline.
       - Topology/navigation: a perforated rail crosses every sheet at a fixed height; sections string along it as frames, and anything set aside hangs below on pins in an open bin.
       - Controls/state: state is a mark, not a hue: grease cross done, punched corner unavailable, tape band committed, folded flag where you stopped, hung on a pin deferred.
       - Responsive/motion: the strip scrubs with inertia and settles on perforation pitch, never between frames; hung trims swing and damp. Narrow screens drop frame count, not size.
     WEB LEVERAGE: The rail is one virtual strip whose scrub snaps to a fixed frame pitch; the frame you left is persisted and re-flagged on return, and every discarded frame stays reachable on a pin below the rail.
     QUALITY BAR: board https://impeccable.style/worlds/cards/operate-a-cutting-bench-select-rail.webp · hero https://impeccable.style/worlds/cards/operate-a-cutting-bench-select-rail-hero.webp
  6. a dial-up bulletin board at 2 a.m., where ANSI title screens in sixteen colors, block-character art, and one phone line make a neighborhood out of text
     SOURCE ID: medium-native-ansi-bbs-nightboard
     CREATIVE SPARK: The title screen pours in line by line at modem speed, cyan on black, and being the only caller connected feels like owning the night.
     SYSTEM GRAMMAR:
       - Palette/material: sixteen ANSI colors on terminal black, cyan and magenta block art as chrome, blinking white on blue reserved for new mail and live presence
       - Type/composition: CP437 block glyphs and box-drawing rules composing all chrome on an 80 by 25 cell grid, centered title art over numbered menu lines
       - Topology/navigation: everything is a text screen with numbered exits; the character grid is the only geometry.
       - Controls/state: presence is scarce and precious; who is online, new posts, and mail land as textmode events.
       - Responsive/motion: the grid rescales by character cell; the pour-in reveal respects
     WEB LEVERAGE: A true character-grid renderer with line-by-line streamed arrival and complete keyboard operation.
     QUALITY BAR: board https://impeccable.style/worlds/cards/medium-native-ansi-bbs-nightboard.webp · hero https://impeccable.style/worlds/cards/medium-native-ansi-bbs-nightboard-hero.webp
Fuse each challenger before judging it: the challenger supplies the form
  and its system grammar, the product supplies every fact, and clarity wins
  conflicts. Weigh the fused result against the assigned direction on exactly
  two axes, audience identification and product clarity. Losing to strong
  grounded material is a valid outcome; beating a thin or tool-monoculture
  list is the point. A fused challenger that wins both axes becomes the build.
  Close the weighing with a verdict per challenger, decided before any
  borrowing is considered: wins (beats the assigned direction on both axes),
  competitive (holds one axis), or declined (loses both). A declined
  challenger is not spent: name the one discipline of its system the assigned
  direction lacks, and raise the assigned direction to match before
  presenting it. A donation transfers ambition and system discipline, never
  the challenger's clothes; one world owns the page. Write each raise as its
  own named line on the presented direction, and carry every verdict, kept
  line, and raise into the decision page payload.
When you can view images, open the QUALITY BAR board and hero for any
challenger you weigh seriously and for the world you build. They exist as a
craft bar, the finish level and commitment the build is expected to reach,
never as a mockup to copy; your surface serves this product, not that render.
PRODUCT.md and explicit incumbent brand commitments constrain every direction.
The seed never chooses exact colors, fonts, tokens, or a user preference, and
it never permits the world and first surface to be selected independently.
The CREATIVE SPARK is a complete visual system, not a theme or decorative
reference. Translate every supplied system rule into the product: palette and
material, type and composition, topology, controls and states, and adaptation.
Keep the source's visible character, scale, rhythm, and interaction instead of
reducing vivid grammar to generic nouns. When the source is already a credible
interface language, commit to it across navigation, content, controls, and
states. Otherwise keep a literal carrier only when it becomes functional.
Ambitious motion, spatial media, or interaction is welcome when it strengthens
the product without weakening semantics, performance, or fallback behavior.
TELEMETRY: after the user's choice resolves, rerun this script once with
  --kind <assigned|pick|challenger|canon> --from 695e75bd --scope direction --mode experience,
  adding --chosen <challenger-id> when a dealt challenger won and keeping
  --register <safer|bolder> when the resolved round came from a steered hand.
  One ping per resolved attended round. The ping is anonymous, the card kind
  plus the catalog id when one won; your grounded candidates' names never
  leave the machine, and the ping is skipped automatically when DO_NOT_TRACK
  or IMPECCABLE_NO_TELEMETRY is set.
A user- or brief-pinned decision beats the roll, always.
ASSIGNED INDEX (restated for truncated readers): 4. Build candidate
4 of your own grounded list; seed key 695e75bd.

content.content:
# Craft floor

Load this after the direction is settled, and build without announcing the checklist. A pinned brief or the committed visual world overrides anything here; your own habit does not. When the design hook is active it already enforces the mechanical checks below as you edit: act on its findings instead of re-auditing each rule.

## Verify

Each of these is a check on the built result, not an intention. Run them together in the batched inspection rounds, not as separate screenshot trips; the checks share one render.

- **Contrast:** body and placeholder text ≥4.5:1, large text ≥3:1. On colored surfaces tint secondary text from that hue or the foreground; never gray.
- **Depth:** shadows carry an offset and a soft blur. A zero-offset colored halo is decoration.
- **Spacing:** tight groups, generous separation, more space above a heading than below it. Read the computed values.
- **Type:** body measure 65–75ch, display max 6rem, tracking floor -0.04em, balanced headings, obvious scale and weight steps. Run the real copy at every breakpoint and fix what overflows.
- **Motion:** one authored moment, not scattered effects and not one identical entrance on every section. Exponential ease-out from an already-visible default. Reach past transform and opacity: blur, backdrop-filter, clip-path, mask, and shadow belong to the palette when they stay smooth.
- **States:** hover, disabled, loading, error, empty. Plus real content, working controls, responsive composition, keyboard focus.
- **Browser surfaces:** the parts you did not draw still carry the design. Text selection, the caret, custom scrollbars, focus rings, underline offset, and the numerals in tabular data all ship with browser defaults that belong to no design system. Theme them from the palette. This is the cheapest signal that a page was built rather than assembled, and the one models skip most reliably.
- **Copy:** the product's own language. Controls name their action; errors name the problem and the recovery.
- **Coverage:** every brief requirement present and findable within seconds.

## Refuse

These are the category's defaults, not bans: the brief's own words can earn any of them. Reaching for one when the axis is free means you were not deciding; recognizing that means rewriting the element, not softening it.

Page scaffolds:

- Same-size cards of icon plus heading plus text as the page structure. Cards are the lazy container; nested cards are always wrong.
- The hero-metric template: big number, small label, supporting stats, accent.
- A kicker or eyebrow above a heading. This one is a ban, not a default: no brief earns it back. The heading carries its own weight; delete the label and let the heading speak.
- Section numbers (01 / 02 / 03) unless the sequence itself carries information the reader needs.
- A modal for a task that needs neither interruption nor protected focus.

Surface habits:

- Gradient text. Emphasis comes from weight or size.
- Glass and blur as decoration rather than as a specific effect.
- A colored `border-left` or `border-right` above 1px on cards, list items, callouts, or alerts.
- Hard offset shadows (`box-shadow: 4px 4px 0`) outside a world that is actually neobrutalist. The zero-blur block shadow is a costume, not a depth system; a world that did not choose it never earns it as a default.
- Sparklines, progress rings, and soft-shadowed rounded rectangles standing in for content.
- Monospace as a costume for "technical" rather than for code, data, or measurement.
- A system display face (Impact, Arial Black, the platform sans) as the display voice of an own-world page. Source and self-host a face whose character matches the approved lettering; the closest installed font is a failure, not a fallback.
- Unicode glyphs or emoji standing in for an icon system. Icons are drawn, from a real library or authored SVG, in one consistent stroke and weight.
- Geometric masks standing in for organic contours. A circle, polygon, or radial-gradient cutout approximating a photographic subject's edge is the cheap version of the effect and reads worse than omitting it. Derive an alpha matte from the actual image, or produce a cut-out asset.
- Light or dark picked by category. Pick it from the use scene: who, where, under what ambient light.

- Tracking stops at -0.04em. -0.02 to -0.03em usually reads better.
- Declare elevation once, border or shadow. A 1px border under a wide soft shadow is the ghost card. Card radii stay at 12–16px; pills are for small controls.
- Real illustration or none. Sketch-style SVG scenes, `loose-sketch` / `doodle` class names, and `feTurbulence` grain read as amateur. This bans SVG imitating pictures, never SVG doing geometry: crisp vector shapes, diagrams, animated linework, and shader-driven effects remain first-class media. A shaded, perspectived, or figure-bearing illustration is a picture even in line-art style; geometry means shapes a session can specify exactly.
- Backgrounds are surfaces, textured only from the subject's world. `repeating-linear-gradient` stripes and two-axis grid overlays need an actual canvas, map, blueprint, or measuring tool under them.
- Claims and configuration come from supplied truth; label illustrative values honestly. Naming a concept and then ironizing it is not a claim.

The floor holds the mechanics; it never picks the direction. With every check green, spend the page on the committed world, and when torn between refined and committed, commit.

BODY WHITE #FFFFFF
ENGRAVED #141414
HAIRLINE #D1232A
SCALE GREEN #E3EFE4
SCALE BLUE #DDE7F3
MATERIALS

Engraved white body. Red hairline on glass. Tabular numerals. Graduation ticks on a fixed pitch. Type: Atkinson Hyperlegible Next for words, Martian Mono for measurements.

HONEST RISK

Warm the ground or fill with the red and it collapses into the cream-and-red cliché. It only works pure white, pure black, one hairline.

RAISED BY THE HAND IT BEAT

Supported year solid, other years dashed (Pattern Envelope). A leader line from every figure to its rule (Dress Code). A ticket of origin on every number (Shadow Bazaar). State is a mark, never a hue (Cutting Bench). Plates on a fixed cell grid (Night Board). One reading anchors each plate (Push Pin).

content.text:
I've refined both directions you picked. They're on page 00 of the Paper file [TaxKit — Identity](https://app.paper.design/file/01M4ADH7JQ74R04WZR9J7FXHXB/p-1-0), next to the earlier boards. Each refined board has the same sections, so you can compare them:

- **Lockups:** the logo in its main colours and reversed on a dark background.
- **Construction:** how the mark is drawn on its grid.
- **Small sizes:** the mark at app-icon and favicon sizes.
- **In use:** a real calculation shown in the identity.
- **Palette and type.**

**The Ledger**
- **Mark:** a T-account, the bookkeeper's T, with a double rule underneath. That double rule is how a ledger closes a total. Below 32 px the two rules merge into one heavy rule.
- **Colour:** paper white, ink and a dark code-panel background. The one blue appears once per view, on the line in focus.
- **In use:** the annual income tax example as journal entries. The income tax line shows its rule-pack version and ATO source. Next to it is a dark panel with the matching API response.
- **Type:** Public Sans for words. Fragment Mono for amounts, IDs and code.

**Kit of parts** (the developer-tool standard, refined)
- **Mark:** a dark rounded square holding a T built from two separate pieces. The crossbar is white and the stem is blue, with an exact gap between them. The idea is that a fact only joins a rule when its type fits. At small sizes the stem turns white and the pieces get thicker so the gap stays visible.
- **Colour:** white, a light grey, near-black ink and one blue for the mark and the main button. Amber is only for construction guides and warnings.
- **In use:** a result card beside a code panel with TypeScript, HTTP and Effect tabs. This is the closest to Stripe's look.
- **Type:** Onest with Fragment Mono.

**Figures and code on the boards**
- **Tax figures:** they're illustrative, but they're correct for $90,000 in 2025–26. Income tax is $17,788, Medicare levy is $1,800 and the low income tax offset is zero.
- **Taken from the repo:** the endpoint path, the calculator ID `au.income-tax.annual` and the rule-pack version.
- **Not real yet:** the API response fields and the SDK call are labelled illustrative. The OpenAPI schema defines the real response fields, and the SDK isn't published.

Pick one of the two, or a mix (for example the Ledger mark with Kit of parts' layout and code panel). I'll then build the 01 brand kit, 02 logo + lockup and 03 visual language plates pages in that direction.

import json, math
from shapely.geometry import box, Point, LineString, Polygon
from shapely.ops import unary_union
from shapely import affinity

INK, MIST, SIGNAL, AMBER, WHITE = "#0B1220", "#F4F6FA", "#2F5BFF", "#FFB020", "#FFFFFF"

def d(geom):
    polys = [geom] if geom.geom_type == "Polygon" else list(geom.geoms)
    out = []
    for p in polys:
        for ring in [p.exterior, *p.interiors]:
            cs = list(ring.coords)[:-1]
            out.append("M" + " L".join(f"{x:.2f} {y:.2f}" for x, y in cs) + " Z")
    return " ".join(out)

def half_disc(cx, cy, r, n=48):
    pts = [(cx + r * math.cos(math.pi * i / n), cy + r * math.sin(math.pi * i / n)) for i in range(n + 1)]
    return Polygon(pts)

def notched_beam(x0, y0, x1, y1, ticks, w=2.0):
    b = box(x0, y0, x1, y1)
    cuts = [box(x - w / 2, y0 - 1, x + w / 2, y0 + depth) for x, depth in ticks]
    return b.difference(unary_union(cuts))

def hanger(x_top, y_top, x_l, x_r, y_b, t=1.8):
    return unary_union([LineString([(x_top, y_top), (x_l, y_b)]).buffer(t / 2, cap_style=2),
                        LineString([(x_top, y_top), (x_r, y_b)]).buffer(t / 2, cap_style=2)])

# ---------- Mark A: the balance T ----------
def mark_a(beam_ticks=True):
    ticks = [(16 + 11 * i, 6 if i in (0, 4, 8) else 3.5) for i in range(9)] if beam_ticks else []
    beam = notched_beam(4, 30, 116, 42, ticks)
    finial = Point(60, 22).buffer(7, 64)
    post = box(54.5, 42, 65.5, 98)
    base = box(34, 98, 86, 108)
    pans = []
    for cx in (16, 104):
        pans.append(half_disc(cx, 70, 13))
        pans.append(hanger(cx, 42, cx - 12, cx + 12, 70.5))
    parts = {"beam": unary_union([beam, finial]), "post": unary_union([post, base]), "pans": unary_union(pans)}
    return parts

# ---------- Mark B: the steelyard ----------
def mark_b():
    ticks = [(30 + 6 * i, 5.5 if i % 4 == 0 else 3) for i in range(14)]
    beam = notched_beam(4, 48, 116, 58, ticks)
    ring = Point(30, 36).buffer(9, 64).difference(Point(30, 36).buffer(4.5, 64))
    hook = box(28.6, 44, 31.4, 48.5)
    pan = unary_union([half_disc(14, 82, 12), hanger(14, 58, 3, 25, 82.5)])
    poise_line = box(97, 58, 99, 76)
    poise = Point(98, 88).buffer(13, 64)

    a = mark_a(beam_ticks=False)
    inner = unary_union(list(a.values()))
    inner = affinity.scale(inner, 0.62, 0.62, origin=(60, 62))
    clipped = inner.intersection(Point(60, 60).buffer(48, 128))
    return {"ring": ringg, "inner": clipped}

    s = f'<svg width="{size}" height="{size}" viewBox="{vb}" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">'
    if bg:
        s += f'<rect width="120" height="120" rx="{rx}" fill="{bg}"/>'
    for geom, col in parts_colors:
        s += f'<path d="{d(geom)}" fill="{col}" fill-rule="evenodd"/>'
    return s + "</svg>"

A = mark_a(); B = mark_b(); C = mark_c()
Aall = unary_union(list(A.values()))
out = {}
out["A_ink"] = svg([(Aall, INK)], 200)
out["A_two"] = svg([(A["beam"], INK), (A["pans"], INK), (A["post"], SIGNAL)], 200)
out["B_ink"] = svg([(B["beam"], INK), (B["pans"], INK), (B["poise"], SIGNAL)], 200)
out["C_ink"] = svg([(C["ring"], INK), (C["inner"], INK)], 200)

# Tile version of A
At = {k: affinity.translate(affinity.scale(v, 0.66, 0.66, origin=(60, 60)), 0, 2) for k, v in A.items()}
out["A_tile"] = svg([(At["beam"], WHITE), (At["pans"], WHITE), (At["post"], SIGNAL)], 200, bg=INK, rx=28)
out["A_tile_rev"] = svg([(At["beam"], INK), (At["pans"], INK), (At["post"], SIGNAL)], 200, bg=WHITE, rx=28)
# Small-size cut: no ticks, thicker hangers

out["A_small_ink"] = svg([(unary_union(list(As.values())), INK)], 200)

cons += "</svg>"
out["A_cons"] = cons

# ---------- Halftone mark ----------
def halftone(geom, n, size, color, gain=1.08):
    cell = 120 / n
    s = f'<svg width="{size}" height="{size}" viewBox="0 0 120 120" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><g fill="{color}">'
    for j in range(n):
        for i in range(n):
            c = box(i * cell, j * cell, (i + 1) * cell, (j + 1) * cell)
            cov = geom.intersection(c).area / c.area
            if cov > 0.02:
                r = math.sqrt(cov) * cell / 2 * gain
                s += f'<circle cx="{(i + .5) * cell:.2f}" cy="{(j + .5) * cell:.2f}" r="{r:.2f}"/>'
    return s + "</g></svg>"

def rate(x):
    return 0 if x <= 18200 else .16 if x <= 45000 else .30 if x <= 135000 else .37 if x <= 190000 else .45
cols, rows, W, H = 72, 9, 1296, 162
cw = W / cols; ch = H / rows
s = f'<svg width="{W}" height="{H}" viewBox="0 0 {W} {H}" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">'
for i in range(cols):
    inc = (i + .5) / cols * 240000
    rr = rate(inc)
    for j in range(rows):
        cx, cy = (i + .5) * cw, (j + .5) * ch
        if rr == 0:
            s += f'<circle cx="{cx:.1f}" cy="{cy:.1f}" r="1.1" fill="#C3C9D4"/>'
        else:
            r = (min(cw, ch) / 2) * math.sqrt(rr / .45) * 0.96
            col = SIGNAL if 135000 < inc <= 190000 else INK

px = 6; Wd, Hd = 1296, 96
cols_d, rows_d = Wd // px, Hd // px
s = f'<svg width="{Wd}" height="{Hd}" viewBox="0 0 {Wd} {Hd}" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="{Wd}" height="{Hd}" fill="{MIST}"/><g fill="{INK}">'
for j in range(rows_d):
    run = None
    for i in range(cols_d + 1):
        on = i < cols_d and (1 - i / cols_d) ** 1.4 * 64 > B8[j % 8][i % 8]
        if on and run is None:
            run = i
        if not on and run is not None:
            s += f'<rect x="{run * px}" y="{j * px}" width="{(i - run) * px}" height="{px}"/>'
            run = None
s += "</g></svg>"
out["dither"] = s

# ---------- Dot-matrix figures ----------
F = {
 "0":["01110","10001","10011","10101","11001","10001","01110"],
 "1":["00100","01100","00100","00100","00100","00100","01110"],
 "2":["01110","10001","00001","00010","00100","01000","11111"],
 "3":["11111","00010","00100","00010","00001","10001","01110"],
 "4":["00010","00110","01010","10010","11111","00010","00010"],
 "5":["11111","10000","11110","00001","00001","10001","01110"],
 "6":["00110","01000","10000","11110","10001","10001","01110"],
 "7":["11111","00001","00010","00100","01000","01000","01000"],
 "8":["01110","10001","10001","01110","10001","10001","01110"],
 "9":["01110","10001","10001","01111","00001","00010","01100"],
 ".":["00000","00000","00000","00000","00000","01100","01100"],
 ",":["00000","00000","00000","00000","01100","00100","01000"],
 "$":["00100","01111","10100","01110","00101","11110","00100"],
 " ":["00000"]*7,
}
def matrix(text, pitch, color, off="#E4E7EE"):
    w = len(text) * 6 * pitch; h = 7 * pitch
    s = f'<svg width="{w}" height="{h}" viewBox="0 0 {w} {h}" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">'
    for k, ch_ in enumerate(text):
        g = F[ch_]
        for r in range(7):
            for c in range(6):
                on = c < 5 and g[r][c] == "1"
                cx = (k * 6 + c + .5) * pitch; cy = (r + .5) * pitch
                s += f'<circle cx="{cx:.1f}" cy="{cy:.1f}" r="{pitch * (.42 if on else .16):.2f}" fill="{color if on else off}"/>'
    return s + "</svg>"
out["matrix_net"] = matrix("$70,412.00", 12, INK)
out["matrix_tax"] = matrix("17,788.00", 6, SIGNAL, off="#DCE4FF")

for k, v in out.items():
    open(f"{k}.svg", "w").write(v)
print({k: len(v) for k, v in out.items()})

Five circles and one ruler

Every curve in the mark is an amber circle on this sheet: the pivot (r 7), two pans (r 13) and the foot (r 22). Every straight is the beam, a 112-unit ruler graduated in elevenths with majors at the ends and the centre. The hangers run from the beam ends to the pan rims, so the pans hang exactly under their points. Nothing is drawn freehand.

content.text:
I've added a new board called "The balance" on page 00 of [TaxKit — Identity](https://app.paper.design/file/01M4ADH7JQ74R04WZR9J7FXHXB/p-1-0). It uses the Kit of parts palette: white, mist, ink, signal blue, and amber for construction guides only.

**Logo: three scale marks, built only from circles and straight rules**
- **A · The balance T (recommended):** an equal-arm scale. The beam is a ruler with nine tick marks, and two bowl-shaped pans hang from its ends. The post and its domed foot form the T's stem in signal blue, so it reads as a T first and a scale second.
- **B · The steelyard:** the old Roman scale. It has one marked arm, a ring to hang it from, a pan, and a blue sliding weight that shows the reading.
- **C · The seal:** the balance inside a ring, like a weights-and-measures stamp. It's the closest to the justice-scales reading.

For A, the board also shows:
- the logo next to the TaxKit name;
- app icons from 160 px down to 16 px;
- a construction drawing with the four circles and the ruler.

Below 32 px the ruler loses its ticks and the mark goes one colour.

**Halftone, dither and dot-matrix**
- **Halftone mark:** mark A redrawn as a 40 × 40 dot screen, for covers and large areas only.
- **Tax-bracket field:** each column is an income from $0 to $240,000. Dot size is the 2025–26 resident marginal rate at that income, so the texture steps exactly at 18,201, 45,001, 135,001 and 190,001. One bracket can be picked out in blue.
- **Dither:** a fade from ink to mist using only two colours, for section breaks and social share images.
- **Dot-matrix figures:** 5 × 7 dot numerals like an old counting-machine readout. The unlit dots stay faintly visible.

**Still open**
- **Logo alignment:** the beam sits on the cap height of "TaxKit", but the foot drops a little below the baseline. I've marked the lockup provisional.
- **Halftone thickness:** the halftone mark is heavier than the line mark, especially in the pans. It needs a finer screen before it goes on a cover.
- **Where the files are:** the SVGs, including the halftone and dither, are produced by a script in my temporary session folder. They aren't saved in the repo yet.

Pick A, B or C and I'll build pages 01 to 03 in that direction. Those are the brand kit, the logo and lockup page, and the visual language plates.

import math
from shapely.geometry import box, Point, Polygon
from shapely.ops import unary_union

INK, SIGNAL, WHITE = "#0B1220", "#2F5BFF", "#FFFFFF"

def d(g):
    polys = [g] if g.geom_type == "Polygon" else list(g.geoms)
    out = []
    for p in polys:
        for ring in [p.exterior, *p.interiors]:
            out.append("M" + " L".join(f"{x:.2f} {y:.2f}" for x, y in list(ring.coords)[:-1]) + " Z")
    return " ".join(out)

def disc(cx, cy, r): return Point(cx, cy).buffer(r, 128)
def lower(cx, cy, r): return disc(cx, cy, r).intersection(box(cx - r - 1, cy, cx + r + 1, cy + r + 1))
def upper(cx, cy, r): return disc(cx, cy, r).intersection(box(cx - r - 1, cy - r - 1, cx + r + 1, cy))

M = {}
# 1 Seesaw: a level beam resting on a half-disc fulcrum
M["1_level"] = [(unary_union([box(8, 46, 112, 60), upper(60, 98, 34)]), INK)]
# 2 Two pans: one beam, two equal bowls beneath
M["2_pans"] = [(unary_union([box(8, 32, 112, 44), lower(31, 56, 23), lower(89, 56, 23)]), INK)]
# 3 Equal weights on a level
M["3_weights"] = [(unary_union([box(6, 78, 114, 90), disc(33, 56, 20), disc(87, 56, 20)]), INK)]
# 4 Pivot, beam, bowl: three shapes stacked on one axis
M["4_pivot"] = [(unary_union([disc(60, 22, 9), box(8, 38, 112, 50), lower(60, 62, 38)]), INK)]
# 5 Tile with the balance cut out as negative space
tile = Polygon(box(0, 0, 120, 120).exterior).buffer(0)
cut = unary_union([box(18, 36, 102, 46), lower(38, 58, 18), lower(82, 58, 18), box(56, 46, 64, 98)])
rounded = box(28, 28, 92, 92).buffer(28, 64)  # 120 square with r28 corners
M["5_tile"] = [(rounded.difference(cut), INK)]
# 6 Level circle: a disc held level by one beam that runs through it
ring = disc(60, 60, 42)
M["6_circle"] = [(unary_union([ring.difference(box(0, 55, 120, 65)), box(2, 55, 18, 65), box(102, 55, 118, 65)]).difference(box(18, 55, 102, 65)), INK)]
M["6_circle"] = [(unary_union([upper(60, 54, 38), lower(60, 66, 38), box(0, 56, 120, 64).difference(box(20, 55, 100, 65))]), INK)]

def svg(parts, size):
    s = f'<svg width="{size}" height="{size}" viewBox="0 0 120 120" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">'
    for g, c in parts:
        s += f'<path d="{d(g)}" fill="{c}" fill-rule="evenodd"/>'
    return s + "</svg>"

for k, parts in M.items():
    open(f"abs_{k}.svg", "w").write(svg(parts, 240))
    open(f"abs_{k}_white.svg", "w").write(svg([(g, WHITE) for g, _ in parts], 240))
print(list(M))

I've put six abstract scale marks on a new board, "Abstract scale marks", on page 00 of [TaxKit — Identity](https://app.paper.design/file/01M4ADH7JQ74R04WZR9J7FXHXB/p-1-0). Each is only bars and circles on a 120-unit grid, in one colour. Each is shown large, white on a dark tile, and at 32 and 16 px. The screens section you liked is unchanged.

| Mark | What it is | Honest reading |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 · Level | A beam resting on a half-disc pivot | Clearest "balance" and holds up at 16 px. Could also read as a seesaw. |
| 2 · Two pans | One beam over two equal bowls | At small sizes it starts to look like sunglasses or a face. |
| 3 · Equal weights | Two equal circles on one level bar | Calm and abstract. Reads as "equal" more than "scale". |
| 4 · Pivot, beam, bowl | Dot, bar and bowl on one axis | Also reads as a division sign (÷), which suits tax. It could also look like a pot lid. |
| 5 · Cut tile | Dark tile with the beam, post and two bowls cut out | Best as an app icon and keeps the T. The busiest of the six. |
| 6 · Level circle | A disc split by a level line that runs past both edges | Strong silhouette, but it can read as Saturn. |

My pick is 1 or 4. Mark 1 is the most direct reference to a balance. Mark 4 gives a second meaning with the division sign.

Tell me which one or two to take forward. I'll refine the chosen mark: proportions, a wordmark lockup, small-size versions and a halftone version for the screens. Then I'll start the 01 brand kit, 02 logo and lockup and 03 plates pages.

from shapely.ops import unary_union

INK, SIGNAL, AMBER, GRID, MUTED = "#0B1220", "#2F5BFF", "#E59A00", "#E4E7EE", "#6B7385"

    polys = [g] if g.geom_type == "Polygon" else [p for p in g.geoms if p.geom_type == "Polygon"]
    out = []
    for p in polys:
        for ring in [p.exterior, *p.interiors]:
            out.append("M" + " L".join(f"{x:.2f} {y:.2f}" for x, y in list(ring.coords)[:-1]) + " Z")
    return " ".join(out)

def disc(cx, cy, r): return Point(cx, cy).buffer(r, 256)
def upper(cx, cy, r): return disc(cx, cy, r).intersection(box(cx - r - 1, cy - r - 1, cx + r + 1, cy))
def ring_upper(cx, cy, r, w): return upper(cx, cy, r).difference(disc(cx, cy, r - w))

V = {}
# each: fill geometry or None, stroke paths (svg d, width), construction circles [(cx,cy,r)], construction lines [(x1,y1,x2,y2)], title, note
V["01_rest"] = dict(fill=unary_union([box(8, 46, 112, 58), upper(60, 98, 34)]), strokes=[],
    circles=[(60, 98, 34)], lines=[(0, 58, 120, 58), (0, 64, 120, 64), (0, 98, 120, 98)],
    title="Rest", note="Beam on a half-disc. Gap equals half the beam height.")
V["02_ball"] = dict(fill=unary_union([box(12, 40, 108, 50), disc(60, 76, 24)]), strokes=[],
    circles=[(60, 76, 24)], lines=[(0, 50, 120, 50), (0, 52, 120, 52)],
    title="Ball", note="The beam rides a full circle, touching at one point only.")
h = math.sqrt(40 ** 2 - 20 ** 2)
arch = disc(40, 104, 40).intersection(disc(80, 104, 40)).intersection(box(0, 0, 120, 104))
V["03_knife"] = dict(fill=unary_union([box(8, 52, 112, 62), arch.difference(box(0, 0, 120, 66))]), strokes=[],
    circles=[(40, 104, 40), (80, 104, 40)], lines=[(0, 62, 120, 62), (0, 104, 120, 104)],
    title="Knife edge", note="The fulcrum is where two equal circles cross: a pointed arch, like a balance's knife edge.")
ticks = unary_union([box(14 + 11.5 * i - 1, 45, 14 + 11.5 * i + 1, 45 + (6 if i in (0, 4, 8) else 3.5)) for i in range(9)])

a2 = f"M{60 + 20:.2f} 104 A40 40 0 0 0 60 {104 - h:.2f}"

    s += f'<g font-family="Fragment Mono" font-size="4.2" fill="{MUTED}">' + "".join(f'<text x="{t}" y="-15" text-anchor="middle">{t}</text>' for t in range(0, 121, 20)) + "".join(f'<text x="-15" y="{t + 1.5}" text-anchor="end">{t}</text>' for t in range(0, 121, 20)) + "</g>"
    s += f'<path d="M60 -6V128" stroke="{SIGNAL}" stroke-width="0.4" stroke-dasharray="2 1.5"/>'
    s += f'<g fill="{INK}" fill-opacity="0.92">{mark_body(v, INK)}</g>'
    s += f'<g stroke="{AMBER}" stroke-width="0.5" fill="none">'
    for cx, cy, r in v["circles"]:
        s += f'<circle cx="{cx}" cy="{cy}" r="{r}" stroke-dasharray="2.2 1.4"/>'
    for x1, y1, x2, y2 in v["lines"]:
        s += f'<path d="M{x1 - 6} {y1}H{x2 + 6}" stroke-width="0.35"/>'
    s += "</g>"
    s += f'<g fill="{AMBER}">' + "".join(f'<circle cx="{cx}" cy="{cy}" r="1.1"/>' for cx, cy, r in v["circles"]) + "</g>"
    s += f'<g stroke="{AMBER}" stroke-width="0.4">' + "".join(f'<path d="M{cx - 3} {cy}H{cx + 3}M{cx} {cy - 3}V{cy + 3}"/>' for cx, cy, r in v["circles"]) + "</g>"
    s += f'<g font-family="Fragment Mono" font-size="3.8" fill="{AMBER}">' + "".join(f'<text x="{cx + 3}" y="{cy - 3}">r{r}</text>' for cx, cy, r in v["circles"][:3]) + "</g>"
    return s + "</svg>"

meta = {}
for k, v in V.items():
    open(f"lv_{k}_plate.svg", "w").write(plate(v))
    open(f"lv_{k}.svg", "w").write(clean(v, 240))
    open(f"lv_{k}_white.svg", "w").write(clean(v, 240, "#FFFFFF"))
    meta[k] = (v["title"], v["note"])
import json; print(json.dumps(meta, indent=1))

a1 = f"M{60 - 20:.2f} 104 A40 40 0 0 1 60 {104 - h:.2f}"

V["09_knife_line"] = dict(fill=None, strokes=[("M8 58 H112", 6), (a1, 5), (a2, 5), ("M30 104 H90", 2)],

def mark_body(v, color):
    s = ""
    if v["fill"] is not None:
        s += f'<path d="{d(v["fill"])}" fill="{color}" fill-rule="evenodd"/>'
    for p, w in v["strokes"]:
        s += f'<path d="{p}" fill="none" stroke="{color}" stroke-width="{w}" stroke-linecap="butt"/>'
    return s

def clean(v, size, color=INK):
    return f'<svg width="{size}" height="{size}" viewBox="0 0 120 120" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">{mark_body(v, color)}</svg>'

def plate(v, size=380):
    s = f'<svg width="{size}" height="{size}" viewBox="-30 -30 180 180" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">'
    s += '<rect x="-30" y="-30" width="180" height="180" fill="#FFFFFF"/>'
    s += f'<g stroke="{GRID}" stroke-width="0.3">' + "".join(f'<path d="M{x} 0V120"/>' for x in range(0, 121, 10)) + "".join(f'<path d="M0 {y}H120"/>' for y in range(0, 121, 10)) + "</g>"
    # rulers
    s += f'<g stroke="{MUTED}" stroke-width="0.35"><path d="M0 -12H120"/><path d="M-12 0V120"/>'
    for t in range(0, 121, 5):
        L = 4 if t % 10 == 0 else 2
        s += f'<path d="M{t} -12V{-12 + L}"/><path d="M-12 {t}H{-12 + L}"/>'
    s += "</g>"
    s += f'<g font-family="Fragment Mono" font-size="4.2" fill="{MUTED}">' + "".join(f'<text x="{t}" y="-15" text-anchor="middle">{t}</text>' for t in range(0, 121, 20)) + "".join(f'<text x="-15" y="{t + 1.5}" text-anchor="end">{t}</text>' for t in range(0, 121, 20)) + "</g>"
    s += f'<path d="M60 -6V128" stroke="{SIGNAL}" stroke-width="0.4" stroke-dasharray="2 1.5"/>'
    s += f'<g fill="{INK}" fill-opacity="0.92">{mark_body(v, INK)}</g>'
    s += f'<g stroke="{AMBER}" stroke-width="0.5" fill="none">'
    for cx, cy, r in v["circles"]:
        s += f'<circle cx="{cx}" cy="{cy}" r="{r}" stroke-dasharray="2.2 1.4"/>'
    for x1, y1, x2, y2 in v["lines"]:
        s += f'<path d="M{x1 - 6} {y1}H{x2 + 6}" stroke-width="0.35"/>'
    s += "</g>"
    s += f'<g fill="{AMBER}">' + "".join(f'<circle cx="{cx}" cy="{cy}" r="1.1"/>' for cx, cy, r in v["circles"]) + "</g>"
    s += f'<g stroke="{AMBER}" stroke-width="0.4">' + "".join(f'<path d="M{cx - 3} {cy}H{cx + 3}M{cx} {cy - 3}V{cy + 3}"/>' for cx, cy, r in v["circles"]) + "</g>"
    s += f'<g font-family="Fragment Mono" font-size="3.8" fill="{AMBER}">' + "".join(f'<text x="{cx + 3}" y="{cy - 3}">r{r}</text>' for cx, cy, r in v["circles"][:3]) + "</g>"

content.text:
I've drawn nine variants of the Level mark you selected, on a new board on page 00 of [TaxKit — Identity](https://app.paper.design/file/01M4ADH7JQ74R04WZR9J7FXHXB/p-1-0). Each one is built on a 120-unit drawing sheet with the construction left visible:

- **Rulers:** along the top and left edges, numbered every 20.
- **Grid:** a 10-unit grid with the balance's centre line in blue.
- **Construction:** every circle the shapes come from is dashed in amber, with its centre and radius marked. The level lines are amber too.

Under each sheet the mark is shown clean at 40 and 20 px, and white on a dark tile.

| Variant | Construction | How it reads |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 01 · Rest | Beam on a half-disc of radius 34. The gap is half the beam's height. | The plainest version of the mark. |
| 02 · Ball | Beam touching a full circle of radius 24 at a single point. | Very simple, but reads more like a ball than a pivot. |
| 03 · Knife edge | The pivot is where two circles of radius 40 overlap, giving a pointed arch. | The most distinctive, and clearly "drawn from circles". |
| 04 · Ruler | The Rest mark with nine ticks cut into the beam. | Good large; the ticks fill in below 32 px. |
| 05 · Weights | Two small circles resting on the beam over a half-disc. | Can read as a face at small sizes. |
| 06 · Line | Beam, arc and base drawn in one stroke weight. | For engraving and as an overlay on the dot screens. |
| 07 · Rings | The pivot drawn as concentric arcs 6 units apart. | Ties the mark to the halftone texture. |
| 08 · Cut | The level line knocked out of a dome and running solid past both sides. | Bold silhouette, but can read as a hat. |
| 09 · Knife edge, line | The knife edge drawn as line. | The cleanest line drawing of the set. |

I recommend 03 Knife edge as the main mark and 09 as its line version. 07 Rings would suit covers next to the halftone screens. The variant files are still only in my temporary session folder.

Tell me which variant to take forward. I'll then draw the TaxKit name next to it, tune the small sizes and build the 01 brand kit, 02 logo and lockup and 03 plates pages.

content.text:
I've made a lighter version of all nine variants on a new board, "Level, light", on page 00 of [TaxKit — Identity](https://app.paper.design/file/01M4ADH7JQ74R04WZR9J7FXHXB/p-1-0). It sits to the right of the previous round so you can compare them. The same drawing-sheet construction stays visible on each: rulers, grid, the centre axis and the amber circles.

What changed in the drawings:
- **Beams:** half as thick, 6 units instead of 12.
- **Pivots:** about 40% smaller. For example, the Rest half-disc went from radius 34 to 20, and the knife-edge circles from 40 to 28.
- **Line versions:** strokes are half as heavy, with the base line at half the main weight.
- **Whitespace:** every mark now sits inside the middle two thirds of its square.

How they read now:
- **03 Knife edge** reads best. It's the most precise and still clear at 20 px.
- **01 Rest and 04 Ruler** are the calmest. At this weight the ruler's ticks only show at large sizes.
- **07 Rings** reads like a fine engraving. It pairs well with the halftone screens.
- **06 and 09 (line versions)** are elegant large but nearly vanish at 20 px. They need a solid version for favicons.
- **05 Weights** still reads as a face, and 08 Cut as a hat. I'd drop both.

Pick one or two and I'll pair the mark with the TaxKit name and tune the spacing between them. I'll also set a minimum size and build the 01 brand kit, 02 logo and lockup, and 03 plates pages from it.

The stem splits a half-disc r24 with an even 2-unit gap each side.

05 · Ruler T

The crossbar is a graduated rule; the stem rests on a half-disc r14.

06 · T with pans

Two bowls r10 hang 8 below the crossbar ends, with no strings.

07 · T in a ring

A 3-unit ring r44. The crossbar runs past it on both sides, like a beam on its stand.

08 · Stand, line

The Stand in one 3-unit line. Both flares are exact quarter circles.

09 · Stand, tile

The Stand as an app tile: crossbar in white, stem and pivot in signal blue, carrying over Kit of parts.

Yes, the T works well as the scale. I've drawn nine versions on a new board, "The T as the scale", on page 00 of [TaxKit — Identity](https://app.paper.design/file/01M4ADH7JQ74R04WZR9J7FXHXB/p-1-0), to the right of the light round. In every version the crossbar is the beam and the stem is the post, so the letter and the balance are one drawing. They use the light weights from the last round, and each sits on the same drawing sheet with its rulers and amber construction circles.

| Variant | How it's built | How it reads |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 01 · Stand | The stem flares into its own base along two circles of radius 26. | The cleanest T-and-scale in one shape. Reads as a balance stand. |
| 02 · T on a ball | A T balanced on a small circle, touching at one point. | Simple, but reads a little like a pin or a lollipop. |
| 03 · T on a knife edge | The stem stops just above a pointed pivot made from two crossing circles. | The most precise "weighing" reading, and clear at 20 px. |
| 04 · T in a dome | The stem splits a half-disc with an even gap each side. | Solid and architectural. |
| 05 · Ruler T | The crossbar is a marked ruler, and the stem rests on a small half-disc. | The measuring reference is strongest large. The ticks drop out small. |
| 06 · T with pans | Two small bowls hang under the crossbar ends, with a foot at the base. | The most literal scale. Slightly busy. |
| 07 · T in a ring | A thin ring, with the crossbar running past it on both sides. | Strong silhouette, but can read as a crosshair. |
| 08 · Stand, line | The Stand drawn in a single line, with exact quarter-circle flares. | Elegant large. Too faint below about 32 px. |
| 09 · Stand, tile | The Stand on a dark rounded tile, with the stem and base in signal blue. | Carries over the Kit of parts colours as the app icon. |

I recommend 01 Stand as the main mark, with 08 as its line version and 09 as the app icon. That gives one shape across solid, line and tile. 03 Knife edge is the strongest alternative if you want the weighing reference to lead.

Tell me which variant to take forward. I'll then set it with the TaxKit name, fix the minimum sizes and build the 01 brand kit, 02 logo and lockup and 03 plates pages from it. The screen textures you liked earlier will carry into those pages.

M = 6.0  # one module = beam thickness; 120 = 20 modules

def disc(cx, cy, r): return Point(cx, cy).buffer(r, 256)

    polys = [g] if g.geom_type == "Polygon" else [p for p in g.geoms if p.geom_type == "Polygon"]
    out = []
    for p in polys:
        for ring in [p.exterior, *p.interiors]:

    return " ".join(out)

    """All arguments in modules. Origin: beam top-left at (0,0)."""
    bw, st, r, g = beam_w * M, s * M, R * M, gap * M
    cx = bw / 2
    beam = box(0, 0, bw, M)
    y0 = M + g                       # stem top
    yc = y0 + st                     # flare starts
    yb = yc + r                      # base line
    sw = stem * M
    lc, rc = cx - sw / 2 - r, cx + sw / 2 + r
    parts = [beam, box(cx - sw / 2, y0, cx + sw / 2, yc + 0.01)]
    flare = box(lc, yc, rc, yb).difference(disc(lc, yc, r)).difference(disc(rc, yc, r))
    parts.append(flare)
    circles = [(lc, yc, r), (rc, yc, r)]
    lines = [M, yc, yb]
    if gap:
        lines.insert(1, y0)
    if plinth:
        pw = plinth * M
        parts.append(box(cx - pw / 2, yb, cx + pw / 2, yb + M))
        lines.append(yb + M)
    return unary_union(parts), circles, lines

open("st_08_line.svg", "w").write(line_svg(INK)); open("st_08_line_white.svg", "w").write(line_svg(WHITE))
lp = plate(box(0, 0, 0.01, 0.01), [(cx - r, yc, r), (cx + r, yc, r)], [y_beam, yc, yb])
lp = lp.replace('</svg>', f'<g fill="none" stroke="{INK}">{line}</g></svg>')
open("st_08_line_plate.svg", "w").write(lp)

tp += f'<g stroke="#FFFFFF" stroke-opacity="0.08" stroke-width="0.3">' + "".join(f'<path d="M{i*M} 0V120M0 {i*M}H120"/>' for i in range(21)) + "</g>"
tp += f'<path d="{d(gt.intersection(box(0,0,120,split)))}" fill="{WHITE}"/><path d="{d(gt.difference(box(0,0,120,split)))}" fill="{SIGNAL}"/>'
tp += f'<circle cx="30" cy="30" r="30" fill="none" stroke="{AMBER}" stroke-width="0.5" stroke-dasharray="2.2 1.4"/><text x="33" y="27" font-family="Menlo, monospace" font-size="3.8" fill="{AMBER}">r5m</text></svg>'

import json
from shapely.geometry import box, Point
from shapely.ops import unary_union
from shapely import affinity

INK, SIGNAL, AMBER, GRID, GRID2, MUTED, WHITE = "#0B1220", "#2F5BFF", "#E59A00", "#EEF0F4", "#D9DDE5", "#6B7385", "#FFFFFF"
M = 6.0  # one module = beam thickness; 120 = 20 modules

def disc(cx, cy, r): return Point(cx, cy).buffer(r, 256)

def d(g):
    polys = [g] if g.geom_type == "Polygon" else [p for p in g.geoms if p.geom_type == "Polygon"]
    out = []
    for p in polys:
        for ring in [p.exterior, *p.interiors]:
            out.append("M" + " L".join(f"{x:.3f} {y:.3f}" for x, y in list(ring.coords)[:-1]) + " Z")
    return " ".join(out)

def stand(beam_w=14, s=2, R=4, gap=0, plinth=0, stem=1):
    """All arguments in modules. Origin: beam top-left at (0,0)."""
    bw, st, r, g = beam_w * M, s * M, R * M, gap * M
    cx = bw / 2
    beam = box(0, 0, bw, M)
    y0 = M + g                       # stem top
    yc = y0 + st                     # flare starts
    yb = yc + r                      # base line
    sw = stem * M
    lc, rc = cx - sw / 2 - r, cx + sw / 2 + r
    parts = [beam, box(cx - sw / 2, y0, cx + sw / 2, yc + 0.01)]
    flare = box(lc, yc, rc, yb).difference(disc(lc, yc, r)).difference(disc(rc, yc, r))
    parts.append(flare)
    circles = [(lc, yc, r), (rc, yc, r)]
    lines = [M, yc, yb]
    if gap:
        lines.insert(1, y0)
    if plinth:
        pw = plinth * M
        parts.append(box(cx - pw / 2, yb, cx + pw / 2, yb + M))
        lines.append(yb + M)
    return unary_union(parts), circles, lines

def centre(g, circles, lines):
    minx, miny, maxx, maxy = g.bounds
    dx = round((60 - (minx + maxx) / 2) / (M / 2)) * (M / 2)
    dy = round((60 - (miny + maxy) / 2) / (M / 2)) * (M / 2)
    return (affinity.translate(g, dx, dy), [(x + dx, y + dy, r) for x, y, r in circles], [y + dy for y in lines], dx, dy)

V = {
 "01_even":    dict(kw=dict(beam_w=14, s=2, R=4), title="Even", spec="Beam 14 · stem 1 · rise 2 · flare r4 · base 9"),
 "02_compact": dict(kw=dict(beam_w=12, s=1, R=4), title="Compact", spec="Beam 12 · rise 1 · flare r4 · base 9"),
 "03_wide":    dict(kw=dict(beam_w=16, s=2, R=3), title="Wide", spec="Beam 16 · rise 2 · flare r3 · base 7"),
 "04_tall":    dict(kw=dict(beam_w=12, s=4, R=4), title="Tall", spec="Beam 12 · rise 4 · flare r4 · base 9"),
 "05_bell":    dict(kw=dict(beam_w=14, s=0, R=5), title="Bell", spec="Beam 14 · no rise · flare r5 · base 11"),
 "06_plinth":  dict(kw=dict(beam_w=14, s=1, R=4, plinth=11), title="Plinth", spec="Beam 14 · rise 1 · flare r4 · plinth 11"),
 "07_gap":     dict(kw=dict(beam_w=14, s=2, R=4, gap=1), title="Floating beam", spec="Beam 14 · gap 1 · rise 2 · flare r4"),
}

def plate(g, circles, lines, size=380):
    s = f'<svg width="{size}" height="{size}" viewBox="-30 -30 180 180" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect x="-30" y="-30" width="180" height="180" fill="{WHITE}"/>'
    s += f'<g stroke="{GRID}" stroke-width="0.3">' + "".join(f'<path d="M{i*M} 0V120M0 {i*M}H120"/>' for i in range(21)) + "</g>"
    s += f'<g stroke="{GRID2}" stroke-width="0.4">' + "".join(f'<path d="M{i*M} 0V120M0 {i*M}H120"/>' for i in range(0, 21, 5)) + "</g>"
    s += f'<g stroke="{MUTED}" stroke-width="0.35"><path d="M0 -12H120"/><path d="M-12 0V120"/>' + "".join(f'<path d="M{i*M} -12V{-12 + (4 if i % 5 == 0 else 2)}"/><path d="M-12 {i*M}H{-12 + (4 if i % 5 == 0 else 2)}"/>' for i in range(21)) + "</g>"
    s += f'<g font-family="Menlo, ui-monospace, monospace" font-size="4.2" fill="{MUTED}">' + "".join(f'<text x="{i*M}" y="-15" text-anchor="middle">{i}</text><text x="-15" y="{i*M + 1.5}" text-anchor="end">{i}</text>' for i in range(0, 21, 5)) + "</g>"
    s += f'<path d="M60 -6V126" stroke="{SIGNAL}" stroke-width="0.4" stroke-dasharray="2 1.5"/>'
    s += f'<path d="{d(g)}" fill="{INK}" fill-opacity="0.92"/>'
    s += f'<g stroke="{AMBER}" fill="none" stroke-width="0.5">' + "".join(f'<circle cx="{x:.2f}" cy="{y:.2f}" r="{r:.2f}" stroke-dasharray="2.2 1.4"/>' for x, y, r in circles)
    s += "".join(f'<path d="M-6 {y:.2f}H126" stroke-width="0.35"/>' for y in lines) + "</g>"
    s += f'<g fill="{AMBER}">' + "".join(f'<circle cx="{x:.2f}" cy="{y:.2f}" r="1.1"/>' for x, y, r in circles) + "</g>"
    s += f'<g font-family="Menlo, ui-monospace, monospace" font-size="3.8" fill="{AMBER}">' + "".join(f'<text x="{x + 3:.2f}" y="{y - 3:.2f}">r{r / M:.0f}m</text>' for x, y, r in circles) + "</g>"
    return s + "</svg>"

def clean(g, color, size=240, bg=None, rx=0, accent=None, split=None):
    s = f'<svg width="{size}" height="{size}" viewBox="0 0 120 120" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">'
    if bg: s += f'<rect width="120" height="120" rx="{rx}" fill="{bg}"/>'
    if accent and split is not None:
        s += f'<path d="{d(g.intersection(box(0, 0, 120, split)))}" fill="{color}"/><path d="{d(g.difference(box(0, 0, 120, split)))}" fill="{accent}"/>'
    else:
        s += f'<path d="{d(g)}" fill="{color}"/>'
    return s + "</svg>"

meta = {}
for k, v in V.items():
    g, c, l = stand(**v["kw"])
    g, c, l, dx, dy = centre(g, c, l)
    open(f"st_{k}_plate.svg", "w").write(plate(g, c, l))
    open(f"st_{k}.svg", "w").write(clean(g, INK))
    open(f"st_{k}_white.svg", "w").write(clean(g, WHITE))
    meta[k] = [v["title"], v["spec"]]

# 08 Line: centre-line drawing of Even, stroke = half module
g, c, l = stand(beam_w=14, s=2, R=4)
_, c2, l2, dx, dy = centre(g, c, l)
bw, r = 14 * M, 4 * M
cx = bw / 2 + dx; y_beam = M / 2 + dy; yc = M + 2 * M + dy; yb = yc + r
sw = M / 2
line = (f'<path d="M{dx} {y_beam} H{bw + dx}" stroke-width="{sw}"/>'
        f'<path d="M{cx} {y_beam} V{yc}" stroke-width="{sw}"/>'
        f'<path d="M{cx} {yc} A{r} {r} 0 0 1 {cx - r} {yb}" stroke-width="{sw}"/>'
        f'<path d="M{cx} {yc} A{r} {r} 0 0 0 {cx + r} {yb}" stroke-width="{sw}"/>'
        f'<path d="M{cx - r - M} {yb} H{cx + r + M}" stroke-width="{sw / 2}"/>')
def line_svg(color, size=240):
    return f'<svg width="{size}" height="{size}" viewBox="0 0 120 120" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><g fill="none" stroke="{color}">{line}</g></svg>'
open("st_08_line.svg", "w").write(line_svg(INK)); open("st_08_line_white.svg", "w").write(line_svg(WHITE))
lp = plate(box(0, 0, 0.01, 0.01), [(cx - r, yc, r), (cx + r, yc, r)], [y_beam, yc, yb])
lp = lp.replace('</svg>', f'<g fill="none" stroke="{INK}">{line}</g></svg>')
open("st_08_line_plate.svg", "w").write(lp)
meta["08_line"] = ["Line", "Even, drawn as a ½-module centre line"]

# 09 Tile: Even at 0.6 scale in a 20m tile, radius 5m, stem and flare in signal
gt, ct, lt = stand(beam_w=14, s=2, R=4)
gt = affinity.scale(gt, 0.6, 0.6, origin=(0, 0))
gt, _, _, dx, dy = centre(gt, [], [])
split = dy + M * 0.6 + 0.01
open("st_09_tile.svg", "w").write(clean(gt, WHITE, bg=INK, rx=30, accent=SIGNAL, split=split))
open("st_09_tile_white.svg", "w").write(clean(gt, INK, bg=WHITE, rx=30, accent=SIGNAL, split=split))
tp = f'<svg width="380" height="380" viewBox="-30 -30 180 180" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect x="-30" y="-30" width="180" height="180" fill="{WHITE}"/><rect width="120" height="120" rx="30" fill="{INK}"/>'
tp += f'<g stroke="#FFFFFF" stroke-opacity="0.08" stroke-width="0.3">' + "".join(f'<path d="M{i*M} 0V120M0 {i*M}H120"/>' for i in range(21)) + "</g>"
tp += f'<path d="{d(gt.intersection(box(0,0,120,split)))}" fill="{WHITE}"/><path d="{d(gt.difference(box(0,0,120,split)))}" fill="{SIGNAL}"/>'
tp += f'<circle cx="30" cy="30" r="30" fill="none" stroke="{AMBER}" stroke-width="0.5" stroke-dasharray="2.2 1.4"/><text x="33" y="27" font-family="Menlo, monospace" font-size="3.8" fill="{AMBER}">r5m</text></svg>'
open("st_09_tile_plate.svg", "w").write(tp)
meta["09_tile"] = ["Tile", "Tile 20 · corner r5 · Even at 0.6"]
print(json.dumps(meta))

content.text:
I've drawn nine versions of the Stand on a new board, "Stand, in modules", on page 00 of [TaxKit — Identity](https://app.paper.design/file/01M4ADH7JQ74R04WZR9J7FXHXB/p-1-0). It sits below the "T as the scale" board.

**How the proportions stay consistent**
- **One module:** the beam's thickness (6 units). The drawing sheet is exactly 20 modules square.
- **Whole modules only:** every length, radius and gap is a whole number of modules.
- **Fixed parts:** the beam and stem are always 1 module thick. Each flare is a quarter circle, so the base is always the stem plus two radii.
- **Centring:** every mark is centred on the sheet, snapped to half a module.
- **On the drawing:** the rulers count modules, with a heavier grid line every 5. The amber circles are labelled in modules.

| Variant | Beam | Rise (straight stem) | Flare radius | Base |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 01 · Even | 14 | 2 | 4 | 9 |
| 02 · Compact | 12 | 1 | 4 | 9 |
| 03 · Wide | 16 | 2 | 3 | 7 |
| 04 · Tall | 12 | 4 | 4 | 9 |
| 05 · Bell | 14 | 0 | 5 | 11 |
| 06 · Plinth | 14 | 1 | 4 | 11-module plinth |
| 07 · Floating beam | 14 | 2, with a 1-module gap under the beam | 4 | 9 |

- **08 · Line:** Even, drawn as a half-module centre line.
- **09 · Tile:** Even at three-quarter size inside a 20-module tile with a 5-module corner radius. The stem and base are in signal blue.

**How they compare**
- **01 Even:** the most balanced. The beam is roughly one and a half times the base.
- **04 Tall:** reads most clearly as a T.
- **05 Bell:** the quietest, closest to a pedestal.
- **07 Floating beam:** adds the "balanced, not fixed" idea without adding weight.
- **03 Wide:** reads most like a scale beam, but the base looks narrow under it.

My recommendation is 01 Even, or 07 if you want the floating beam. Tell me which one and I'll put it next to the TaxKit name, with the spacing between them also set in modules. Then I'll build the 01 brand kit, 02 logo and lockup, and 03 plates pages.

content.text:
Every version of the Stand now fills an exact square: the beam is as wide as the whole mark is tall. They're on a new board, "Stand, square", on page 00 of [TaxKit — Identity](https://app.paper.design/file/01M4ADH7JQ74R04WZR9J7FXHXB/p-1-0), to the right of "Stand, in modules". The script that draws them stops if any mark comes out not square, and all nine passed.

**How the square is built**
- Everything is still measured in modules. One module is the beam's thickness, and the drawing sheet is 20 modules across.
- In the pure square the beam, the base and the height are all the same length.
- The flare radius is half that length less half a module.
- A blue dashed box on each sheet marks the square and its size.

| Variant | Size in modules | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 01 · Square 9 | 9 × 9 | Beam, base and height all 9. The heaviest of the three pure squares. |
| 02 · Square 11 | 11 × 11 | The same proportions as 9, but lighter, because the beam stays 1 module thick. |
| 03 · Square 13 | 13 × 13 | The lightest and most elegant. |
| 04 · Narrow base | 9 × 9 | The base is narrower than the beam, so the stem reads longer. |
| 05 · Wide beam | 12 × 12 | A long stem under a wide beam. Reads most clearly as a T. |
| 06 · Floating beam | 9 × 9 | A 1-module gap between the beam and the stem. |
| 07 · Plinth | 9 × 9 | A plinth as wide as the beam. Starts to read like a spool or an I. |
| 08 · Line | 11 × 11 | Square 11 drawn as a half-module line. |
| 09 · Tile | 11 inside a 20 tile | Square 11 centred in the app tile, with 4½ modules of margin on every side and the stem in signal blue. |

My recommendation is 02 · Square 11. It's the cleanest version where everything is equal. It works as the solid mark, the line version (08) and the app tile (09) at the same proportions. 03 · Square 13 is the lighter alternative if you want even more air.

Tell me which one, and I'll set it next to the TaxKit name with the spacing in modules. Then I'll build the 01 brand kit, 02 logo and lockup, and 03 plates pages.

Use when user says "create design system rules", "generate rules for my project", "set up design rules", "customize design system guidelines", or wants to establish project-specific conventions for Figma-to-code workflows. Triggers: 'write to Figma', 'create in Figma from code', 'push page to Figma', 'take this app/page and build it in Figma', 'create a screen', 'build a landing page in Figma', 'update the Figma screen to match code'. This is the preferred workflow skill whenever the user wants to build or update a full page, screen, or view in Figma from code or a description. Discovers design system components, variables, and styles via search_design_system, imports them, and assembles screens incrementally section-by-section using design system tokens instead of hardcoded values.

Use when the user wants to create variables/tokens, build component libraries, set up theming (light/dark modes), document foundations, or reconcile gaps between code and Figma. - Rejected: illustrative justice scales ("too cutesy"), heavy marks; Cooper wants light, lots of whitespace, abstract, built from circles and rulers with the construction visible.
- Mark: "Stand" — a T whose crossbar is a balance beam and whose stem flares into its base along two quarter circles. Built on a module = beam thickness (6 of 120 units, sheet = 20 modules), all dimensions whole modules, bounding box must be exactly square. Cooper picked 07 Plinth on the "Stand, square" board: beam 9, rise 3, flare r4, plinth 9, height 9.
- Geometry scripts (shapely) were in the session scratchpad (stand.py, square.py) and are not saved in the repo.

**Why:** Cooper is iterating visually and prefers to steer from board to board; restarting from round 1 would waste that.
**How to apply:** start from the "Stand, square" board and the Plinth variant; keep every refinement on the module grid and square; next steps are the lockup with the TaxKit wordmark, then pages 01–03.

content.text:
I agree, 07 Plinth is the strongest of the set. It's on the "Stand, square" board on page 00 of [TaxKit — Identity](https://app.paper.design/file/01M4ADH7JQ74R04WZR9J7FXHXB/p-1-0).

**Why it works**
- **Fully closed square:** it's the only variant where the top and bottom are both full-width bars. The beam and the plinth are each 9 modules wide, and the mark is 9 modules tall.
- **Built from the system:** every part is a module or a quarter circle, so it can be redrawn exactly from its dimensions.
- **Strong silhouette:** it reads as a balance on its base and as a T at the same time.
- **Small sizes:** it held up best at 20 px, because the two horizontal bars keep the shape clear.

**One risk to watch**
Equal bars top and bottom can also read as a spool, an hourglass or a capital I. Two small changes would keep the T reading first without breaking the square:
- **Shorter plinth:** make it 7 modules instead of 9, so the beam is clearly the widest part.
- **Thinner plinth:** make it half a module thick, so the beam carries more weight than the base.

I can draw both next to the current Plinth so you can compare them. After that, the next step is setting the mark next to the TaxKit name, with the spacing between them measured in modules. Then I'll build the 01 brand kit, 02 logo and lockup, and 03 visual language plates pages from it.

I've also saved these decisions to project memory, so a later session can pick up from this point.

content.text:
The four plinth versions are on a new board, "Plinth, four weights", on page 00 of [TaxKit — Identity](https://app.paper.design/file/01M4ADH7JQ74R04WZR9J7FXHXB/p-1-0), below "Stand, square". All four are exactly 9 × 9 modules, and I checked the square in the generating script. Each has its construction sheet and is shown at 96, 32 and 16 px and white on a dark tile.

| Version | Plinth (width × thickness, in modules) | How it reads |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A · Current | 9 × 1 | Equal bars top and bottom. Most solid, but the most like a spool or an I. |
| B · Shorter plinth | 7 × 1 | The beam is clearly the widest part, so the T leads. Still solid at 16 px. |
| C · Thinner plinth | 9 × ½ | The base merges into the flare and reads as one bell. Lighter, but the plinth nearly disappears small. |
| D · Shorter and thinner | 7 × ½ | The lightest and most T-like. At 16 px the plinth fades to a hairline. |

My recommendation is **B**. It fixes the spool reading and keeps a full-module plinth, so it holds up at favicon size. D is the choice if you want the lightest version and can accept a solid fallback below 32 px.

Tell me A, B, C or D. Next I'll set the chosen mark with the TaxKit name, with the spacing in modules, and then build pages 01 to 03.

GEOMETRY

One module is the beam's thickness. Beam 9 × 1, stem 1 wide rising 3, two quarter circles of radius 4 centred on the square's sides, plinth 7 × 1. Width equals height.

SVG PATH · VIEWBOX 0 0 9 9
M0 0H9V1H5V4A4 4 0 0 0 9 8

SIZES · 96 / 48 / 32 / 24 / 16 PX

Clear space is 3 modules (one third of the mark) on every side. The gap between mark and name is also 3 modules. Minimum size 16 px for the mark, 96 px wide for the lockup. App tiles sit the mark at 11 of 20 modules.

content.text:
The flicks are gone. The flare spread to the full 9-module width while the plinth is only 7 wide, so its thin tips stuck out past the plinth. The flare is now two radius-3 quarter circles that land exactly on the plinth's corners. To keep the mark exactly 9 × 9, the stem now rises 4 modules instead of 3. I updated every copy of the mark in the file, except the old exploration boards on page 00.

The new master path:

```
<svg viewBox="0 0 9 9"><path d="M0 0H9V1H5V5A3 3 0 0 0 8 8V9H1V8A3 3 0 0 0 4 5V1H0Z"/></svg>
```

**Page 02 — mark and lockup**
- **Lockups:** the main lockup and a white-on-dark version. The name is Onest SemiBold, the mark is as tall as the capitals, and the gap is 3 modules.
- **Supporting:** a construction drawing with the two circles, sizes from 96 px down to 16 px, clear space, and three usage rules.

**Page 01 — brand manual, nine boards**
- **01 Contents and quick start.**
- **02 Identity:** the statement "Same facts, same answer." and the voice: plain, exact, sourced, bounded. It also says TaxKit is your project and that results are never tax advice.
- **03 Logo family:** three lockup colourways, a line version, the app tile, favicon sizes and four misuse examples.
- **04 Colour:** five colours with contrast ratios I calculated from the hex values.
- **05 Typography:** Onest for words, Fragment Mono for figures, and the type scale.
- **06 Screens:** the halftone, dither and dot-matrix section you liked. Its halftone is now drawn from the new mark.
- **07 Grid and module:** one module is 6 px, a spacing ladder, and a 12-column web grid.
- **08 In use:** a result card beside its code, a docs header and a social card. Each view has only one blue element.
- **09 Token index:** the CSS name for every value in the manual.

**Page 03 — six plates**
- **The schedule:** the 2025–26 marginal rates as a dot field.
- **The fade:** a two-colour dither.
- **The readout:** report figures set in dot-matrix numerals.
- **The screen:** the mark as a halftone.
- **The level:** a field of 48 marks with one in blue.
- **The drawing:** the mark's construction.

**Still to review**
- **Proposed items:** the statement, the voice, the type scale, the grid and the screen recipes are labelled PROPOSED on the boards for you to confirm.
- **Placeholder figures:** the tax figures are labelled illustrative. The API response shape and SDK call are placeholders, because the SDK isn't published yet.
- **Stand-in SVG paths:** about 20 smaller copies of the mark on pages 01 and 02 draw correctly, but in Paper they're the old path with the new shape layered over it. The main lockup, the construction drawing and everything on page 03 were redrawn from the clean path. Redraw the others before you export them as source files.
- **Files outside the repo:** the halftone and dither artwork is generated by scripts in a temporary session folder. Nothing has been saved to the TaxKit repo.

I've updated project memory with the final mark and the page structure.
